Quick triage notes from the runtime side (first 20m):
- Observed KV cache size growth on shard-7 and shard-9 starting ~08:40 PT; lookups per second unchanged but cache miss rate is climbing.
- Batching latency distribution shows a longer tail: batch window is occasionally holding for 120ms vs typical 40–60ms under the current policy.
- A small subset of RPCs to the decoder are timing out and cascading into 502 responses at the gateway.

Hypothesis: sudden prefix variance increased KV cache churn and intermittently extended batch formation windows, tripping decoder quad-queue timeouts. There is also a kernel mismatch we saw in the past when sequence length suddenly spikes with our quantized decoder path.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (low-risk first):
1) Reduce max batch wait from 120ms -> 60ms for the affected routes (route id: hawthorne-online-score).
2) Temporarily lower per-request concurrency to reduce decoder pressure (throttle inbound concurrency by 30% for 10m).
3) Enable the non-quantized decoder variant for hot shards if we see continued timeouts (this increases memory usage but reduces decode errors).

I can push the batch wait and concurrency changes as a config override now if Marissa gives the green light. Will also produce a short hotfix plan for rollback.

Jonas Weber
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Jackson / team — we initiated mitigations at 09:42 PT:
- Reduced batch window to 60ms for hawthorne-online-score.
- Applied 30% concurrency throttle on the hot route.
- Enabled fallback model variant for routes with >5% error rate.

Early observations (09:50 PT): p95 improved from ~3.7s -> ~2.5s, 502 rate dropped from 14% -> 6%. Not stable yet but moving in the right direction.

Next steps:
- We're preparing a short hotfix (hotfix_plan.patch) to flip the decoder to non-quantized path on shards 7/9; this should remove the intermittent decoder timeouts.
- We will keep autoscaling enabled but will hold off on adding more nodes until we validate the decode path change.
- Attaching the operational runbook (runbook_v2.pdf) and the hotfix patch. Link to docs: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3C_example_runbook

Can you confirm you have the Drive access and that enabling the non-quantized decoder variant is acceptable on your side (it will increase memory footprint by ~18%)?

Stakeholders —

Summary (timeline):

- 09:42 PT: Redwood applied batch window reduction and route concurrency throttle; initial improvement observed.
- 09:55 PT: Hotfix planned to switch decoders on shard-7/9 to non-quantized path; customer approved.
- 2028-03-02 17:10 PT: After extended validation, we saw a recurrence when sequence-length variance increased during a late-night scoring job. We isolated load to a nightly job and mitigated via temporary job throttling on customer side.

Current status: stable but fragile; 5xxs reduced to <1% and p95 ~1.6s. We have a postmortem in progress and a recommended configuration change to make the non-quantized decoder the default for hawthorne's private cluster (or provide a permanent option to auto-failover before hitting RPC timeouts).

Request for exec decisions / approvals:
- Approve a temporary credit to HawthorneAI for the two-days of elevated failures (proposed credit: one week of reserved capacity equivalent) — this will be discussed with finance.
- Approve a planned maintenance window to make the decoder variant change permanent (expected 45m, low-risk but requires coordination).
- Approve continued dedicated SRE coverage for Hawthorne during the maintenance window.

Attachments: incident runbook and hotfix artifacts; links in metadata. I recommend we schedule a 30-min leadership sync tomorrow morning to finalize credit & maintenance details.

Laura Bennett
